pharm: Steroid hormone precursor; dietary supplement (vaginal prasterone is the approved prescription form)
quick: Supplement: 25-50 mg PO once daily (unregulated); vaginal prasterone 6.5 mg (one insert) nightly
Avoid in liver disease; metabolized hepatically
summary: Dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) is an endogenous adrenal steroid that serves as a precursor to androgens and estrogens. Oral DHEA is sold as a dietary supplement (not FDA-approved as a drug) for proposed uses such as adrenal insufficiency, aging and libido, with limited high-quality evidence. The vaginal form prasterone (Intrarosa 6.5 mg) is FDA-approved for moderate-to-severe dyspareunia of vulvovaginal atrophy in menopause. Key concerns are androgenic/estrogenic effects and use in hormone-sensitive cancers.
indications: Vaginal prasterone (Intrarosa): moderate to severe dyspareunia due to menopausal vulvar and vaginal atrophy (FDA-approved)
Oral DHEA supplement (not FDA-approved): proposed use in DHEA deficiency / adrenal insufficiency replacement
Investigational/supplement use: age-related decline, mood, sexual function (limited evidence)

dosage.d: 6.5 mg (one vaginal insert) once daily at bedtime

dosage.n: Under specialist guidance; monitor DHEA-S levels

admin: Take oral DHEA supplement with food, usually in the morning
Insert vaginal prasterone (Intrarosa) at bedtime using the provided applicator
Supplement product quality and potency are not FDA-standardized - use reputable sources
Periodically reassess the need and monitor for hormonal side effects
Avoid in patients with hormone-sensitive malignancy
moa: DHEA and its sulfate (DHEA-S) are endogenous adrenal steroids that act as precursors converted peripherally into androgens (testosterone) and estrogens (estradiol). Tissue effects depend on local steroidogenic enzyme activity. Vaginal prasterone is converted locally in vaginal cells to estrogens and androgens, restoring vaginal epithelium and reducing dyspareunia with low systemic hormone exposure.

absolute: Known or suspected hormone-sensitive cancer (breast, prostate, endometrial, ovarian)

preg: DHEA is androgenic and its safety in pregnancy is not established; avoid use in pregnancy. Vaginal prasterone is not indicated in pregnancy.
lact: Use is not recommended during breastfeeding due to its androgenic/estrogenic activity and lack of safety data.
hepatic: DHEA is metabolized by the liver; avoid in significant liver disease and use caution given altered steroid metabolism.

major: Hormone-sensitive cancer therapies / aromatase inhibitors - DHEA can counteract estrogen suppression
Estrogen or androgen therapy - additive hormonal effects
moderate: Antiplatelet/anticoagulant agents - theoretical altered platelet effects
Insulin/oral hypoglycemics - may affect glucose handling
minor: Other supplements with hormonal activity - additive effects
interactions.food: Oral supplement is taken with food.
interactions.diagnostics: Raises serum DHEA-S, testosterone and estrogen levels, potentially confounding hormone assays.

emergency: Symptoms suggestive of a hormone-driven malignancy (abnormal bleeding, breast lump)

monitoring: Androgenic effects: acne, hirsutism, voice deepening, scalp hair loss
DHEA-S and sex steroid levels if used for replacement
Screening for and surveillance of hormone-sensitive cancers; abnormal vaginal bleeding (prasterone)
counsel: DHEA oral products are dietary supplements, not FDA-approved medicines; quality and potency vary
Do not use if you have or have had a hormone-sensitive cancer without specialist advice
Report acne, unwanted hair growth, voice changes, mood changes or abnormal vaginal bleeding
Tell your clinician about all supplements and medicines you take
pk: Hormonal effects over days to weeks
DHEA ~15-30 min; DHEA-S much longer (~10-20 h)
Store at room temperature; vaginal inserts refrigerate per label
pearls: NOTE: Oral DHEA is an OTC dietary supplement, NOT an FDA-approved drug; data are from EMA/clinical literature and supplement use - product potency is unregulated
The FDA-approved related product is vaginal prasterone (Intrarosa 6.5 mg) for menopausal dyspareunia
Avoid in hormone-sensitive cancers (breast, prostate, endometrial)
Androgenic side effects (acne, hirsutism, hair loss) are dose-related, especially in women
Can confound hormone assays and counteract aromatase inhibitor therapy
missed: If a dose is missed, take it when remembered unless it is nearly time for the next dose; do not double the dose. For vaginal prasterone, resume the next bedtime insert as scheduled.
overdose: No specific antidote. Excessive intake may produce pronounced androgenic/estrogenic effects (acne, hirsutism, mood and lipid changes). Discontinue and provide supportive care; monitor hormone levels and for cardiovascular effects.
